exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
outcome: Presence and strain-level analysis of Bacteroides and Phocaeicola species
Shared strains between mothers and infants
cohort: 144 mother-infant pairs from the PreventADALL study
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with early colonization of Bacteroides and Phocaeicola species in infants, with specific strains of B. caccae and P. vulgatus being shared between mothers and their vaginally born infants.
mod_finding: Bacteroidaceae members were mainly detected in samples from vaginally delivered infants.
gest_age: Pregnant women recruited at 18 weeks of gestation
